$janet.$comment: Not JSON Schema. Read by scripts/Test-OutputContracts.ps1, which is the point of the file living here rather than being generated from the return type.
$janet.$comment.contract2: 1 -> 2 on 2026-09-03: items gained 'area', the stored project label that show and report can now be narrowed by. A field added to the envelope is a format change, so the number moved and so did the surface below.
$janet.$comment.contract3: 2 -> 3 on 2026-09-04: the envelope gained 'areas', one {area, open} entry per area with open items over the WHOLE list, whatever the area selector narrowed to. Startup now narrows the report to the session's own area (the manifest's run entry passes -Area), and without this map the other projects' backlog would vanish from the brief rather than be summarised. Same rule as contract 2: a field added is a format change. The same bump made items[].notesLead OPTIONAL: narrowing alone left the JanetHome brief at 9,969 characters against a budget of about 8,000, and the leads were 1,827 of the report, so the startup entry now passes -NoLead as well. One bump, two changes, because they landed together.
$janet.$comment.contract4: 3 -> 4 on 2026-09-06: focus became one cursor PER AREA rather than one for the whole list, so 'active' changed meaning and every 'areas' row gained one. The defect: items gained a stored 'area' on 2026-09-03 and the reading verbs gained an 'area' selector, but focus was left global -- the list was partitioned for reading and not for focus, so the sessions running in four repos against this one shared store fought over a single variable. Measured the morning of the bump: the startup brief ran the report with -Area JanetHome, returned 21 JanetHome items, and named a gamehub item beside them as the thing in hand -- the brief that exists to orient a JanetHome session pointed at another repo's work. In the same session, setting a JanetHome item active parked a gamehub session's item twice, and completing a JanetHome item cleared focus for all four areas. So 'active' now names the focus of THIS ANSWER'S SCOPE: the area you narrowed to, or null when you narrowed to nothing, because a scalar cannot carry four cursors and reporting an arbitrary one of them is exactly how the brief came to lie. 'areas[].active' is what makes the unnarrowed answer complete, and it removes the null ambiguity the change would otherwise introduce: 'nothing is in focus anywhere' is every row carrying null, which a reader can tell apart from the envelope's own null, which means 'you did not narrow -- read the map'. NO STORAGE CHANGE and nothing to migrate: status plus the item's area already encoded this, so the one item then active kept focus within its own area and every other area started with none. Same rule as contracts 2 and 3, and the same two files move together.
$janet.$comment.contractField: The envelope stamps 'contract' and the gate cross-checks it against the number above, so code and schema cannot drift apart in either direction. The older thread envelopes carry no such field -- they are pinned by recorded goldens instead -- which is why this one differs from its own family.
$janet.$comment.notShow: Deliberately NOT the thread_show envelope. Show carries items[].notes in full and is asserted byte for byte against output recorded from the pre-shim PowerShell, which the golden generator extracts out of git and re-runs -- so it cannot grow a field without a declared correction. This is a separate format beside it, which is why it needed no correction at all.

contract.description: Bumped only by a format change. An engine change that moves this number is a mistake in one direction; a format change that does not is a mistake in the other.

count.description: Items in this answer. Excludes completed items unless all=true was passed.

active.description: Topic in focus in THIS ANSWER'S SCOPE, or null. Since contract 4 focus is one cursor PER AREA, so this names the cursor of the area you narrowed to and is null whenever you passed no area -- a scalar cannot carry four cursors, and picking one of them to report is what made a brief narrowed to JanetHome name a gamehub item. Null here therefore does NOT mean nothing is in focus; it means this answer was not scoped to an area. Read 'areas' for every cursor at once, and note that nothing active anywhere is an ordinary state either way, not a fault.

areas.description: The map of the WHOLE open list: one entry per area with at least one open item, sorted by area name case-insensitively, computed before either selector -- it describes the list, not this answer. Present whether or not area narrowed, and empty only when nothing is open anywhere. '(unfiled)' appears as a row like any other when unlabelled items are open, and is absent rather than zero when none are. Completed items are never counted, whatever all= says: the map answers where the rest of the backlog is, and finished work is not backlog. Since contract 4 each row also carries that area's cursor, which is what makes an unnarrowed answer complete rather than merely honest about being unscoped.

area.description: The resolved area label, as items[].area spells it, so it can be passed straight back as the area selector.

open.description: Open (active or parked) items filed under this area. Never zero: an area with nothing open has no row.

active.description: The topic this area has in focus, or null where it has none. Focus is one per area since contract 4, so these rows are the complete set of cursors: every row null means nothing is in focus anywhere, which is a different statement from the envelope's own null. Always present, never omitted -- an absent key would make 'no cursor here' and 'this row does not report focus' the same absence, which is the ambiguity the field exists to remove.

notesLength.description: Total characters of note body NOT carried by this envelope, summed across items. Present so the omission is stated rather than implied: an envelope that silently dropped the notes would look complete.

error.description: A list that could not be read, reported in-band because this runs in the startup path. It is a fact about the list, not a failure of the call: a reader that ignores it sees an empty list, which is the honest degraded answer rather than a wrong one.

area.description: Which project or area this item belongs to. A STORED label, never derived from the topic: splitting topics on their first colon was measured to produce 12 groups for 16 topics and to split single projects across several. Always present and never empty -- an item with none reads as the literal '(unfiled)', which is one real group rather than a guess at which project it resembles. Narrow to it with the report's own 'area' selector.

topic.description: Identity. Items are addressed by topic, as a dictionary -- position was removed on 2026-08-14 because the display hides completed items while an index counted into the unfiltered file.

status.description: Focus is one PER AREA since contract 4: at most one item is active within any one area, and several areas can each hold one at the same time. It was at most one across the whole list until 2026-09-06, which is the claim this field's description used to make and which four concurrent sessions sharing this list disproved.

refs.description: research.json node ids. Context that earned a node, as opposed to notes, which is detail too small or too fresh to be worth one.

next.description: The resume cursor: the one thing to do first on return. Carried in FULL, never truncated -- it is the field the report exists to deliver, and abbreviating it would defeat the purpose.

notesLead.description: First NON-EMPTY line of the notes, trimmed, capped at 200 characters with a trailing ellipsis when cut. First non-empty rather than first, because notes built by appending begin with a blank line. OPTIONAL since contract 3: absent (the key, not an empty string) when the caller declined leads -- --no-lead, -NoLead, lead=false -- so that an item with no notes and an item whose lead was withheld cannot be confused. notesLength is carried either way.

notesLength.description: Full size of this item's notes in characters, whether or not any of it is shown. This is how a one-line note is told from a five-day log without carrying either.
